params.body:
A figure from public data, a report or a company's own numbers can now back a claim. It is read at its origin and never counted as a signal. The same version ships the vocabulary as TypeScript types, so engines stop keeping their own copy of the ids.

## Why

The 78 posts on gentells.com now cite 198 sources found in their text. 46 of those sentences carry a figure: 28 are cited at the publisher's own page, 18 at an article or site that reports the figure. Until now a citation could only be a signal, so a Eurostat table and a news story about it were the same kind of evidence. The sources plan (gentells-pipeline `docs/design/sources-before-more-sources.md`) calls for a reference layer where datasets back claims and never become signals, with Eurostat as the pilot. This is that layer's contract.

## What changes

- **Statistic**, a tenth class. It holds:
  - the value and unit
  - what it measures, the population (with ages when the publisher gives them) and the period
  - its basis: official, survey, company or research
  - the publication, the locator (a dataset code, table or page) and the url of the publication itself
  - the passage, the time it was retrieved, and the sample size for a survey
- **Relations:**
  - `publishedBy`: Statistic to Source, exactly one.
  - `restsOnStatistic`: Trend to Statistic, with the same support verdicts as a signal. It is also a cross-link, so a client trend can rest on a Gentells statistic.
  - `statisticSupersededBy`: points from a figure to its revised version.
  - `cites` can now end at a Statistic.
- **States:** current, superseded and withdrawn. Nothing is deleted.
- **`rules/statistic.json`:**
  - **origin:** the figure is read from the publisher's own page.
  - **citable:** the figure must be current, every required field must be present, and a survey needs its sample size. The publisher must be admitted, with terms that allow a paid product. These are the same terms used to admit a source, so a non-commercial dataset such as the European Social Survey is refused.
  - **cohort:** the generation comes from the ages in the last year of the period, and only when the whole range falls within one macro generation.
  - **backing:** a statistic never counts towards a trend's supporting signals, sources, strength or holds.
  - **display:** publisher, publication, locator and period, with a link. A value is never shown without its unit, population and period.
- **`tools/rules.mjs`** adds `statisticCitable` and `statisticCohort`.
- **`tools/validate-graph.mjs`** refuses a cited statistic that may not be cited, and now checks a property's `pattern` and `maxLength`.
- **`tools/check.mjs`** keeps the statistic rules consistent with the class, the states and the relation, and refuses any rule that would let a statistic count towards a trend's numbers.
- **Types:** `exports/gentells-standard.d.ts`, exported as `@trendwolves/gentells-standard/types`. It has:
  - two id types per scheme: the ids an engine may write, and the ids stored data may still carry
  - the states, relation ids and class ids
  - the props and node shape of every class

  It is generated with the other exports, and `export.mjs --check` keeps it fresh.

## Not changed

Evidence kinds still describe signals only. No trend number moves, and nothing stored changes meaning.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 84 of 84 pass. That includes 9 cases on when a statistic may be cited and 7 on who it is about, 4 new conformance graphs, and compatibility with v0.1.0 to v0.11.0.
- The generated types pass `tsc --strict` (TypeScript 5.6.3) against an example that builds a Statistic node and a graph. That check also confirms a retired generation id and an unknown basis are type errors.

After merge: tag `v0.12.0`. Then a pipeline PR pins 0.12.0 and starts `checkJs` on these types.
params.title: Standard 0.12.0: Statistic, a figure read at its origin, plus generated types
